subject: Calamites woody jointed tree with offset branch tiers
factual_scope: Genus-level vegetative Calamites reconstruction using original university fossil collection stem/Annularia photographs and UCMP description of sphenophyte nodal whorls. Associated foliage morphogenus is not a second asset or synonym. Whole outline, tiers/counts, scale and colors are interpretive; no exact organ species association claimed.
identifying_features: One continuous substantial woody main trunk with eight visible nodes; four occupied nodal tiers have five radiating primary branches each, successive tiers azimuthally offset.

Each primary branch bears two jointed secondary twigs, each carrying two seven-leaf whorls of small narrow lanceolate Annularia-like leaves. Keep hierarchy open and clearly different from a grass-sized horsetail cluster.

Trunk outer surface quiet, no fine pith-cast longitudinal ridges asserted as bark. Modest integrated node swellings, no separate floating rings. Sterile whole-habit concept, no cones, flowers, decorative pedestal or roots asserted.

concept_decisions: Concept inspected: retain jointed hierarchy but greatly reduce oversized star foliage and collar-like node swellings. Make leaf whorls small subordinate details on secondary twigs. Outer bark intentionally quiet because longitudinal ribs on consulted casts describe internal mold/pith preservation, not known external bark.

All dimensions are nominal art targets; measured component and whole bounds reported from actual vertices, not echoed config. Closed topology and no zero-area faces required. Foliage and branch attachment inspected; expected overlapping plant joints are permitted, exposed coplanar surface interference is not.
